docs.title: Bia's notes - Four strangers in the Mists
docs.text: Four strangers answered the promise of two hundred gold. Before the job was finished, they would cross a forest after dark, enter a ruined church transformed into an alchemical laboratory, awaken a sixty-five-year-old automaton, conceal a discovery that could threaten the Domains of Dread, and learn that neither their employer nor the inn in which they met was what it seemed.

docs.title: Adventure at a glance
docs.text: Item Details Company Ravenlost Starting Level 1 Ending Level 2 Starting Location The Black Lantern Inn Destination Glim Brightstone's church-turned-alchemical laboratory Employer Henry Loust Patroness Lady Estella Godfroy of the Mordent Godfroys Objective Recover the journal of the missing dwarf alchemist Glim Brightstone Promised Reward 200 gp each Advance Payment 100 gp each Major Encounters Four wolves, animated mechanical body parts, a metal-eating construct, and unknown toe-walking creatures Major Discovery Glim may have created an apparatus capable of breaking a dreadlord's hold over the Mists New Acquaintances Cedgewick and Eva Final Revelation Henry was a spirit, and the Black Lantern Inn appeared to have been abandoned for years

docs.title: Ravenlost
docs.text:
The four adventurers who would come to be known as Ravenlost met for the first time at the Black Lantern Inn.

  • Bia Galene, a six-foot-six female Orc barbarian
  • Cadric Veyl, a three-foot-tall Halfling bard with sandy hair and hazel eyes, weighing only thirty-two pounds
  • Jain Blight, a six-foot-four female Lupine ranger with gunmetal-colored fur, a purple left eye, and a scar crossing her right eye
  • Elisandra Corvis, a six-foot-tall Kalashtar cleric with pure white hair

They arrived as strangers. Each had followed word of a job worth two hundred gold.

By the time they returned, they were not yet friends, but they were beginning to become a company - Ravenlost.

docs.title: Notable moments
docs.text:
• Cadric negotiated one hundred gold up front for every member of the party.
  • Jain consumed four bowls of grog before the group left the inn.
  • The party discovered five-toed footprints with no heel.
  • Ravenlost solved the inscription "Come as one" by crossing the doors while holding hands.
  • Bia screamed when a mechanical arm reached toward her.
  • Jain put a metal-eating construct on a rope as though it were a pet.
  • Cadric's lute attracted the animated body parts rather than calming them.
  • Two of the monsters that shattered the ceiling died upon impact.
  • The party chose to destroy the most dangerous of Glim's recordings.
  • Bia threw the dead treasure hunters outside rather than sleep near them.
  • Henry's witnesses turned out to be the ghosts of those same treasure hunters.
  • Henry walked through his desk and revealed that he, too, was a spirit.
  • The party received its gold and advanced to level 2.
  • The lively inn became a dusty, abandoned building when the office door opened.
  • Jain still searched for grog.
  • Eva entered without being invited.

docs.title: Henry Loust
docs.text: An elderly-seeming gentleman with glasses and in fine-but-worn clothing who hired Ravenlost on behalf of Lady Estella Godfroy. He was later revealed to be incorporeal, though the nature of his connection to the Black Lantern Inn remains unknown.

docs.title: Lady Estella Godfroy
docs.text: Henry's patroness and a member of the Mordent Godfroy family. She wanted Glim Brightstone's journal recovered.

docs.title: Glim Brightstone
docs.text: A dwarf alchemist who disappeared nearly sixty-five years ago. He developed an apparatus that could potentially chart a path through the Mists and break a dreadlord's hold over them.

docs.title: Cedgewick
docs.text: An automaton created by Glim Brightstone. Glim used him to preserve journal entries on wax recording tubes. Much of Cedgewick's memory was deliberately erased.

docs.title: Victor Mordenheim
docs.text: The dreadlord of Lemordia and one of several figures believed to have wanted Glim's apparatus.

docs.title: Wilfred Godfroy
docs.text: The dreadlord of Mordent, toward whose domain Glim charted his final known course.

docs.title: Eva
docs.text: A fortune teller who entered the abandoned Black Lantern Inn immediately after the party discovered its true condition.

docs.title: Wolves
docs.text: A pack of four attacked Ravenlost shortly after Jain answered a distant howl.

docs.title: Animated mechanical remains
docs.text: Separate arms, legs, and torsos that moved independently after the laboratory's systems were activated.

docs.title: Metal-eating construct
docs.text: A small mechanical, animal-like creature attracted to metal and capable of damaging it. Jain temporarily kept it on a rope.

docs.title: Unknown toe-walking creatures
docs.text: Five creatures crashed through the laboratory's stained-glass roof. Their highly arched feet matched the unusual tracks found in the woods and around the bodies. Cedgewick identified them as the work of Victor Mordenheim.

docs.title: Discoveries
docs.text:
• Glim Brightstone stored his journal entries on wax tubes recorded through Cedgewick.
  • Lunar energy could be focused to plot a route through the Mists.
  • A sufficiently charged apparatus might break a dreadlord's control over the fog.
  • The apparatus also affected the physical and spiritual nature of a person.
  • Glim feared his invention and eventually fled north toward Mordent.
  • Someone deliberately erased portions of Cedgewick's memory.
  • Glim had an assistant whose identity is currently unknown.
  • Glim believed woods existed beyond Abbey Point, despite the map ending there.
  • Henry Loust and the two missing treasure hunters were spirits.
  • The Black Lantern Inn may not exist in the ordinary way—or may not have been occupied for many years.

docs.title: Open mysteries
docs.text:
• What happened to Glim Brightstone after he left the laboratory?
  • Who was Glim's assistant?
  • Why were specific portions of Cedgewick's memory erased?
  • What exactly does the apparatus do to a person's body and spirit?
  • Who else sought Glim's invention?
  • Why did Victor Mordenheim send creatures to the laboratory?
  • What lies beyond Abbey Point?
  • Where did the two bodies go during the night?
  • Who—or what—is Henry Loust?
  • How did Henry know what happened in the laboratory?
  • Why did the Black Lantern Inn appear lively before becoming abandoned?
  • What does Eva want with Ravenlost?
  • Who—or what—is Korath?

docs.title: Treasure and advancement
docs.text:
• 200 gp earned by each party member
  • 100 gp paid before departure
  • 100 gp paid upon completion
  • Two intact wax recordings were retained for delivery.
  • The party found alchemical books and copper recording tubes.
  • All four members of Ravenlost advanced from level 1 to level 2.

docs.title: Bia's journal
docs.text:
We left the inn as strangers.

Cadric talked Henry into paying us half before we went. Jain drank four bowls of grog before we even reached the road. Elisandra watched everything and carried her own light into the dark. I carried my axe.

The footprints bothered me. Five toes, but no heel. I had never seen tracks like them, and I didn't like knowing that whatever made them was somewhere ahead of us.

I screamed when the arm reached for me. I will deny this if Cadric writes a song about it.

Cedgewick was not what I expected to find in that place. He had been alone for almost sixty-five years, surrounded by Glim's work and missing pieces of his own memory. We asked him to leave with us, but he couldn't. I understand what it means to be bound to a home, though I don't know whether his bond is loyalty or a cage.

We destroyed three recordings. I think it was the right choice. Knowledge that can tear through the Mists and change a person's soul shouldn't be handed to someone simply because he promises gold.

The ghosts agreed with our story. That was fortunate.

Henry was a ghost too. None of us noticed. Jain noticed the moving pages, but apparently didn't think it worth mentioning until after Henry walked through the table.

We earned our gold. We are stronger now than when we left. I'm not sure whether that means we are ready for what comes next.

When we opened Henry's door, the inn was dead and covered in dust.

Then Eva arrived.

I still don't trust the Mists. I am beginning to think I may trust the others.

docs.title: Looking ahead
docs.text:
The Black Lantern Inn was empty. Dust muffled every step, and the laughter that had filled the taproom moments earlier seemed impossible.

A knock sounded at the door.

No one answered.

The door opened anyway.

Eva the fortune teller stepped out of the Mists and into the abandoned inn.

To be continued.

docs.title: Bia's notes - The shadows of Crawford
Adventure at a glance
docs.text: Starting point: Black Lantern Inn Destination: Mordenshire, Mordent Unexpected stop: Crawford Primary mystery: Multiple people and entire families have disappeared without signs of forced entry or robbery. Main suspect/location: Crawford Mano Other suspicious location: Locust Branch Hospital

docs.title: Madam Eva's reading
docs.text: Madam Eva arrived at the abandoned Black Lantern Inn and performed a card reading.

docs.title: First five cards
docs.text: Card Reading / Notes Mists A journey ahead. The Mists may claim those who aren't careful. Miser A lord rules from a mansion. He refuses to give in to something he fears more than death. Dictator No interpretation given. Beast Cadric pointed at Jain. Darklord No interpretation given.

docs.title: Cards placed over the first reading
docs.text:
• Berserker → Dictator
  • Charlatan → Darklord
  • Shepherd → Beast
  • Ghost → Miser

Cadric believes the cards represent people we already know or will eventually encounter. He’s a smart one.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
• Who unlocked the front door when Madam Eva left?
  • Who is the lord represented by the Miser?
  • Does the Ghost placed over the Miser relate to that lord?
  • Who are the Dictator and Darklord?
  • Is Jain actually connected to the Beast card, or was Cadric just being Cadric?

docs.title: Traveling through the Mists
docs.text:
We decided to head north toward Griffin Hill / Mordenshire in Mordent.

Because visibility was almost nonexistent, we tied ourselves together with rope.

docs.title: Impaled body
docs.text:
We repeatedly encountered a body impaled on a pike.

Cadric examined it and found a falcon branded into the person's chest.

Possible significance: Unknown.

docs.title: Parry's Potables
docs.text:
Met Parry, a traveling potion merchant headed toward Dementlieu.

Notable detail:

  • Wore a jeweled charm shaped like a mask.
  • Confirmed Jain's red vials from the alchemy lab were healing potions.
  • Sold us four additional healing potions.
  • Cadric negotiated a group discount.
  • We also purchased a disguise potion for Jain.

Cadric considered leaving with Parry.

He didn't.

docs.title: Crawford
docs.text:
We emerged from the Mists in a marsh approximately a day and a half from Mordenshire.

Nearby:

  • Crawford
  • Locust Branch Hospital
  • Crawford Mano
  • Pond / river
  • Woods

docs.title: Locust Branch Hospital
docs.text:
Full sign:

Locust Branch Hospital — Condemned under the Act of Death

The hospital appears abandoned but is definitely not empty.

docs.title: Inside
docs.text:
Jain entered through a broken window.

She saw:

  • An abandoned hospital ward.
  • A shiny object beyond swinging doors.
  • A bandaged arm reach through the doors and take the object.

Elisandra used Augury before we went farther inside.

Result: Bad idea.

Bia left.

Jain eventually did too.

docs.title: Lavar
docs.text:
Lavar is one of the hospital guards.

He told us:

  • The hospital is dangerous.
  • Crawford has experienced several recent disappearances.
  • Daverick, the night guard Lavar was replacing, was missing.
  • Daverick should have walked to work.
  • There was a town meeting at the Raven's Claw Inn about the disappearances.
  • Crawford is governed by Sterling Crawford.
  • Sterling has been secluded in Crawford Mano since his pregnant wife became ill.

docs.title: Pablo
docs.text:
Lavar's dog.

Jain talked to him.

Pablo says there are ghosts around the hospital.

Specific example:

  • Every night around 11:00 PM, a ghost named Cynthia throws/slams herself into a hospital window.

Pablo could not smell Daverick along his normal route to work.

He could smell Daverick near the dock.

docs.title: Missing people
docs.text:
According to Thom Youngblood, Crawford's de facto leader:

Missing When Notes Lone Farmer John 9 days ago Lives closest to Crawford Mano. Peterbuild family 5 days ago Husband, wife, and son. Neighbors noticed no smoke from chimney. Stern & Persephone Reynolds Last night Husband and wife. Daverick Discovered today Hospital night guard; also tended Crawford Mano's grounds.

docs.title: Geographic pattern
docs.text:
Moving outward from Crawford Mano:

  1. Lone Farmer John
  2. Peterbuilds
  3. Reynolds
  4. Lemroys / Darrons nearby

The disappearances appear to be moving progressively farther away from the manor.

docs.title: Crawford Manor
docs.text:
Sterling Crawford owns/runs the manor and governs Crawford.

Known information:

  • Sterling's wife became ill during pregnancy.
  • Sterling withdrew into the manor to care for her.
  • The local priest visited when she was approximately 6½ months pregnant.
  • He provided herbs, but they did not help.
  • Sterling then banished him from the manor and decided to care for his wife himself.
  • Mrs. Crawford had previously been pregnant, but the child did not survive.
  • Sterling receives regular shipments from Larder Supply.
  • The most recent shipment disappeared and is now four days overdue.
  • Typical shipments include grain, meat, and linens.
  • Earlier shipments included baby supplies and furniture.
  • Requests for baby items eventually stopped.

docs.title: Thema
docs.text:
Thema is the caretaker at Crawford Mano.

Known information:

  • Gnome.
  • Approximately 300 years old.
  • Roughly Cadric's size/build.
  • Stark white hair.
  • Apparently rules the manor with an iron fist.

docs.title: Daverick's house
docs.text:
Daverick's house was unlocked.

Inside:

  • Humble furnishings.
  • Unmade cot.
  • Back door open.
  • Fine porcelain teapot and cup that seemed far too expensive for Daverick.
  • Tea with a strong, astringent smell.
  • Small white flowers in the teapot.

Outside:

  • Large boot print leading toward/into the river.

The priest identified the flowers as hemlock.

docs.title: Hemlock
docs.text:
• Paralytic.
  • Native only to Echo Island.
  • Same substance later appears to have been used on Cadric.

The priest also agreed that the porcelain looked like something the Crawford family could own.

docs.title: Reynolds' house
docs.text:
Evidence:

  • Two sets of footprints near the river.
  • Same size boot.
  • One set of prints was significantly deeper than the other.
  • Table set for three.
  • Two empty cups.
  • No teapot.
  • Tea residue smelled like the tea at Daverick's.
  • Three strands of hair found:
  • Medium brown
  • Long blonde
  • Stark white

Identifications:

  • Stern Reynolds: medium brown hair
  • Persephone Reynolds: long blonde hair
  • Thema: white hair

This strongly suggests Thema—or someone with matching white hair—was at the Reynolds' house.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
Why were the footprints the same size but different depths?

Was someone carrying another person?

docs.title: Peterbuild’s and John’s houses
docs.text:
Both houses appeared almost untouched.

Lone Farmer John's was especially clean—possibly too clean for such a humble home.

No:

  • Teapot
  • Cups
  • Obvious tea residue
  • Other obvious evidence

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Were these houses cleaned after the victims disappeared?

docs.title: The pond
docs.text: Jain and Bia investigated the pond before nightfall.

docs.title: Jain's discovery
docs.text:
Near where the river current enters the pond, Jain searched the silt and found:

  • Human skull
  • Deep, uneven scrapes on the bone
  • Scrapes did not appear to have been made by metal

Unknown whether the damage occurred before or after death.

docs.title: Bia's discovery
docs.text:
Bia dove into the middle of the pond and recovered a burlap sack weighted down with a rock.

Inside were three additional sacks.

Each contained infant bones.

docs.title: Major questions
docs.text:
• Who were the infants?
  • Are they connected to Mrs. Crawford?
  • Why were their remains dumped in the pond?
  • What caused the damage to the adult skull?
  • How long have the remains been there?

docs.title: Watching the Lemroy house
docs.text: Earnest and Ella Lemroy agreed to stay at the inn while we watched their property.

docs.title: The perfect plan
docs.text:
Because the Lemroys are halflings:

  • Cadric: Disguise himself as Mr. Lemroy and serve as "bait."
  • Jain: Hide under the bed.
  • Elisandra: Watch from the barn and telepathically warn Cadric.
  • Bia: Watch from the barn roof.

It was the perfect plan.

docs.title: The hooded figure
docs.text:
At approximately 11:30 PM, Bia saw a roughly four-foot-tall hooded figure emerge from the woods.

It carried:

  • Kettle
  • Pouch
  • Cup

The figure knocked on the Lemroy door.

Cadric answered.

It offered him a cup and said:

"Drink."

Cadric was magically compelled to obey.

The tea:

  • Tasted vile.
  • Paralyzed him.
  • Appeared to contain hemlock.

The figure entered and whistled.

docs.title: Attack
docs.text:
Bia swung at the figure.

Her axe passed through the cloak.

There was nothing inside it.

The figure disappeared, leaving behind:

  • Kettle containing the remaining tea
  • Lantern

Elisandra heard:

  • Something nearby.
  • Water moving toward the creek/manor.

Jain saw:

  • A black figure flying toward Crawford Mano.

docs.title: Important
docs.text:
The attacker apparently:

  1. Approaches a home.
  2. Offers poisoned tea.
  3. Compels the victim to drink.
  4. Paralyzes the victim.
  5. Summons or signals something.
  6. Somehow transports the victim toward the river/manor.

This may explain the missing families.

docs.title: Cadric vs. hemlock
docs.text:
Cadric remained paralyzed for approximately 15 minutes.

Unfortunately for Elisandra, paralysis did not prevent telepathy.

She briefly considered moving more than twenty feet away so she would no longer have to listen to his complaints and expletives.

Bia eventually put him on the bed.

Apparently, he asked.

docs.title: Shadow attack
docs.text:
During Cadric's watch at approximately 1:30 AM, the room began growing darker.

He turned toward the fire.

There were three shadow figures around it.

Cadric screamed.

Battle followed.

Result:

  • 1 shadow killed.
  • 2 shadows fled.

No further attacks that night.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
Were the shadows connected to:

  • Crawford Mano?
  • The hooded figure?
  • Locust Branch Hospital?
  • Something else entirely?

docs.title: What we know before entering Crawford Mano
docs.text:
Evidence connecting the disappearances to the manor:

  1. Missing households are progressively farther from Crawford Mano.
  2. Daverick also worked on the manor grounds.
  3. Daverick had an expensive porcelain tea service likely associated with the Crawfords.
  4. Daverick's tea contained hemlock.
  5. Reynolds' cups contained similar residue.
  6. White hair found at the Reynolds' house matches Thema.
  7. A hooded figure attempted the same poisoned-tea method at the Lemroy house.
  8. The hooded figure was approximately Thema's size.
  9. After disappearing, something traveled through the water toward the manor.
  10. Jain saw a black figure fly toward Crawford Mano.
  11. Human and infant remains were found in the nearby pond.
  12. Sterling Crawford has isolated himself since his wife's illness and pregnancy.
  13. The Crawfords previously lost another pregnancy.
  14. Baby supplies to the manor abruptly stopped.
  15. The manor's most recent supply shipment has disappeared.

Pablo Lavar's dog; sees ghosts and provided information about Daverick. Cynthia Ghost who reportedly appears at the hospital around 11 PM. Daverick Missing hospital guard; previously worked on Crawford Mano grounds. Thom Youngblood Crawford's de facto community leader. Ron Owner/storekeeper of Larder Supply. Sterling Crawford Lord/governor of Crawford; secluded inside his manor. Mrs. Crawford Sterling's pregnant and seriously ill wife. Thema Elderly gnome caretaker of Crawford Mano; white hair. Stern Reynolds Missing; medium brown hair. Persephone Reynolds Missing; long blonde hair. Earnest & Ella Lemroy Family whose house Ravenlost used to trap the mysterious visitor.

docs.title: Current objective
docs.text:
Thom gave us a rough map of the Crawford Mano grounds and the portion of the house he remembers from childhood.

The townspeople now agree that something nefarious is happening at the manor.

Crawford Mano.

docs.title: Bia's notes - The battle of Crawford Manor
Adventure at a glance
docs.text:
What began as an investigation into Crawford Manor quickly turned into a violent confrontation, a disturbing rescue, and the discovery that something was deeply wrong beneath the manor—and perhaps with Crawford itself.

The party battled a massive man inside the manor, attempted to save the soul of his pregnant wife, and discovered a dumbwaiter leading into underground passages. Following those tunnels brought them into Crawford, where they found frightened villagers, strange behavior, and hints of something supernatural at work.

After gathering what information they could, the group returned to the manor through the tunnels, determined to uncover what was happening.

docs.title: Entering the Manor Grounds
docs.text:
• We travel to Crawford Manor.
  • Cadric finds a section of fence that we can sneak through.
  • Jain discovers a cistern that runs from the manor toward the creek.
  • We sneak through the fence onto the manor grounds.
  • We see a large observatory.
  • Inside the observatory, Cadric sees flower pots containing small white flowers.

docs.title: The Basement
docs.text:
• Cadric unlocks a door leading into the basement.
  • The basement contains:
  • Chests
  • Stacks of supplies
  • Food
  • Clothing
  • Alcohol
  • A ladder leading upward
  • A large chest contains nicer but older clothing.
  • We also find:
  • A raven-feather brooch
  • A silver necklace with sapphires
  • Jain takes the brooch and necklace.
  • Cadric extinguishes the light and climbs the ladder.
  • He quietly opens the door at the top and sees a room lit by candlelight.
  • He comes back down.

docs.title: Exploring the Manor
docs.text:
• Bia climbs the ladder.
  • It opens into what appears to be a servants' kitchen.
  • Bia hears floorboards creaking above her.
  • Someone is walking upstairs.
  • Cadric eventually follows Bia into the kitchen.
  • Jain investigates several rooms on the first floor.
  • She finds a greenhouse, but it does not contain the small white flowers seen in the observatory.
  • Another room contains a dumbwaiter large enough to hold several people.
  • Jain goes to the second floor.
  • She finds:
  • A room with double doors
  • A room with a single door
  • Jain hears faint crying coming from behind the single door.

docs.title: Elisandra's Discovery
docs.text:
• Back in the basement, Elisandra notices a false wall.
  • The wall moves backward when she pushes it.
  • Elisandra enters the pitch-black room carrying her candle.
  • She finds an older human man hanging upside down from a hook.
  • His throat has been slashed.
  • His tongue is missing.
  • He appears dead at first, but is actually still alive.
  • Elisandra continues farther into the room.
  • There are five hanging bodies total.
  • All five are missing their tongues.
  • Most have had their throats cut.
  • At least one has not had his throat cut.
  • Elisandra also finds:
  • Chains belonging to the dumbwaiter/lift
  • The dumbwaiter shaft
  • A lever controlling it

docs.title: Bia Attempts Stealth
docs.text:
• Bia tries to quietly climb the stairs to the second floor.
  • Her foot clips one of the steps.
  • She comes down hard and her foot smashes through the stair.
  • The footsteps above stop.
  • Bia is stuck in the stairs.

docs.title: "Fresh Meat"
docs.text:
• An abnormally enormous man approaches Bia.
  • His arms are huge and covered in dried blood.
  • He looks at Bia and says:

"Fresh meat."

  • Cadric sees Bia on the stairs with the enormous man approaching her, ready to attack.

"Holy fuck."

docs.title: Thema
docs.text:
• Jain enters the room with the single door.
  • Inside is an elderly female gnome crying beside an empty crib.
  • She motions for Jain to be quiet.
  • Jain and the woman whisper to one another.
  • Jain tells her that we want to save Crawford.
  • The woman says we can't save it.
  • She tells Jain to jump out the window and leave.
  • The woman's name is Thema.
  • Thema is the caretaker of Crawford Manor.
  • She has served there for 62 years.
  • Thema identifies the enormous man as what remains of Sterling Crawford.
  • Sterling has gotten larger as his wife has gotten worse.
  • Sterling's wife is Ladna Crawford.
  • Ladna has anemia, and her declining condition has been driving Sterling mad.
  • Ladna's child still hasn't arrived.
  • Thema says the child may never arrive.
  • Thema is trapped inside the house.
  • Jain offers to lower Thema from the window so she can escape.
  • Thema agrees.
  • Jain lowers Thema out the window and then follows her down.

docs.title: Battle with Sterling Crawford
docs.text:
• Sterling kicks Bia down the stairs, freeing her from the broken step.
  • In the basement, Elisandra hears the fighting above.
  • She can hear Cadric singing his attacks.
  • Elisandra stays with the surviving man hanging from the hook.
  • Sterling breaks through the banister and moves to punch Cadric.
  • Cadric uses his luck.
  • Sterling misjudges Cadric's height and swings too high.
  • Sterling's arm becomes lodged in the wall.
  • Cadric attacks him, but the wound barely scratches Sterling.
  • Cadric attacks again and lodges his dagger in Sterling's arm.
  • Bia attacks while Sterling is stuck.
  • She sinks her axe deep into his arm.
  • In the basement, Elisandra pulls the dumbwaiter lever.
  • Outside, Jain attempts to pick the front door lock.
  • She fails.
  • Jain rings the doorbell and waits around the corner.
  • No one answers.
  • Sterling pulls his arm free from the wall.
  • Sterling kicks Cadric down the stairs.
  • Sterling attempts to follow Cadric.
  • Bia gets an opportunity attack.
  • Bia critically slashes Sterling across the back of his neck.
  • Sterling collapses onto the landing in pain.
  • Cadric tries to attack Sterling but misses.
  • In the basement, Elisandra sprinkles holy water on the surviving man.
  • He is too heavy for her to remove from the hook by herself.
  • Outside, Jain sees Thema sprint away.
  • Jain attempts to pick the lock again and fails.
  • She breaks a window and enters the basement.
  • Sterling struggles back to his feet.
  • He attacks Bia twice.
  • Both attacks miss.
  • Sterling screams:

"I WILL NOT LET THEM TAKE HER!"

  • Bia attacks, but her axe slams into the wall.
  • Cadric lands the final killing blow.
  • Sterling Crawford dies.
  • Cadric grabs Sterling's arms and plays with his corpse like a puppet.
  • Cadric notices Sterling is wearing a ring.
  • He cuts off Sterling's finger and takes the ring.

docs.title: Ladna Crawford
docs.text:
• The dumbwaiter reaches the basement.
  • Elisandra notices bloody footprints inside it.
  • Jain finds Elisandra and sees the room containing the hanging bodies.
  • Jain and Elisandra enter the dumbwaiter and ride it upstairs.
  • The entire party meets on the second floor in the room behind the double doors.
  • A very pregnant woman is lying on the bed.
  • She is connected to an IV.
  • The IV is connected to a pulsing red sack of blood.
  • The woman is Ladna Crawford.
  • Elisandra communicates with Ladna telepathically.
  • Ladna tells Elisandra:

"Kill me. My existence is torture."

  • She also says:

"It's not a child of mine anymore."

  • Ladna tells Elisandra that Wilfred Godfroy will come after them in death.
  • Sterling has been keeping Ladna alive to prevent this from happening.
  • If we kill Ladna, she will have 14 hours—until midnight—to be herself again.
  • After that, she will have to take the hallowed march to the house on Griffin Hill.
  • Bia remembers having to kill severely wounded animals on the farm as acts of mercy. She never liked doing it.
  • Jain approaches Ladna.
  • She gently kisses her on the forehead.
  • Jain stabs Ladna through the stomach.
  • Her weapon passes through at least three layers of bone.
  • Ladna dies.
  • Her stomach releases fluid.
  • An unholy creature emerges.
  • The creature:
  • Has many eyes
  • Has a tail
  • Is also dead
  • Cadric finds a hat in the room.
  • Cadric takes the hat.

docs.title: Daverick
docs.text:
• The group returns to the basement.
  • Bia and Elisandra work together to remove the surviving man from the hook.
  • Jain finds a tunnel leading toward the cistern.
  • She crawls into it headfirst.
  • Jain follows the tunnel but finds only a shoe.
  • She returns to the basement.
  • Cadric uses healing magic on the surviving man.
  • The man cannot speak because his tongue has been removed.
  • We believe the man is Daverick.

docs.title: Recovering Our Belongings
docs.text:
• Elisandra searches the room containing the bodies.
  • She finds a chest containing everyone's belongings.
  • Jain also finds:
  • 17 gold
  • 36 silver
  • 12 copper
  • Elisandra finds a bottle of grain whiskey.
  • She drinks the entire bottle on the spot.

docs.title: The Villagers Arrive
docs.text:
• We take Daverick outside.
  • Thema and the villagers are approaching Crawford Manor.
  • The townspeople are extremely happy to see Daverick alive.
  • Thom, the priest, and Ron ask if everything has been handled.
  • We tell them about the bodies hanging in the basement.
  • Thema insists she didn't know the bodies were there.
  • We are dubious.
  • The villagers enter the manor to investigate.
  • One of them comes back outside and vomits.
  • The entire manor is a bloody scene.
  • Cadric helpfully clarifies:

"Also, that guy was already missing a finger."

docs.title: Back at the Inn
docs.text:
• Everyone returns to the inn in Crawford.
  • Thom gives us a room for the night.
  • The townspeople are sad because so many of their friends have died.
  • They are also grateful because they finally feel safe.
  • Cadric performs at the inn.
  • Jain examines the items she took from the manor:
  • Raven-feather brooch: Not magical
  • Sapphire necklace: There is something magical or unusual about it.
  • Cadric examines:
  • His new hat/cap
  • Sterling's ring

docs.title: Midnight
docs.text:
• Ladna told us the dead would be called to Griffin Hill at midnight.
  • At midnight, we go outside to see if the stories are true.
  • In the distance, we see a ripple of greenish-blue light.
  • Orbs travel from Sterling Manor toward the light.
  • We see ghostly figures emerge:
  • Sterling Crawford
  • Ladna Crawford
  • A baby in Ladna's arms
  • Sterling is human again rather than the enormous creature we fought.
  • Ladna is also restored to human form.
  • Sterling and Ladna look back at Crawford Manor.
  • Then the spectral family travels northeast toward Mordenshire and Griffin Hill.

docs.title: Sterling Crawford
docs.text:
• Husband of Ladna Crawford.
  • Had become abnormally enormous.
  • Thema said Sterling grew larger as Ladna's condition worsened.
  • Was increasingly unstable.
  • His arms were covered in dried blood.
  • Extremely difficult to injure.
  • Shouted, "I WILL NOT LET THEM TAKE HER!"
  • Was keeping Ladna alive because of what would happen after her death.
  • Killed by Cadric.
  • Appeared in human form during the hallowed march.

docs.title: Ladna Crawford
docs.text:
• Sterling Crawford's wife.
  • Gravely ill with anemia.
  • Pregnant with something she no longer considered her child.
  • Asked us to kill her.
  • Said her existence was torture.
  • Warned us about Wilfred Godfroy.
  • Said she would have 14 hours after death before being forced to join the hallowed march.
  • Killed by Jain as an act of mercy.
  • An unholy, many-eyed creature was found inside her.
  • Appeared at midnight in human form carrying a baby.

docs.title: Thema
docs.text:
• Elderly female gnome.
  • Caretaker of Crawford Manor.
  • Has served at the manor for 62 years.
  • Was found crying over an empty crib.
  • Helped explain what had happened to Sterling and Ladna.
  • Escaped through a second-floor window with Jain's help.
  • Claims she didn't know about the bodies hidden in the basement.

docs.title: Daverick
docs.text:
• Found hanging upside down in the hidden basement room.
  • Throat was not cut.
  • Tongue had been removed.
  • Rescued by Bia and Elisandra.
  • Healed by Cadric.
  • The people of Crawford were extremely happy to see him alive.

docs.title: Wilfred Godfroy
docs.text:
• Mentioned by Ladna.
  • Ladna said he would come after them in death.
  • Connection to Griffin Hill and the hallowed march is not yet completely clear.

docs.title: Important Items and Clues
docs.text:
• Small white flowers in the observatory
  • Cistern connecting the manor toward the creek
  • Raven-feather brooch
  • Not magical
  • Silver sapphire necklace
  • Appears to be magical or otherwise unusual
  • Sterling's ring
  • Taken by Cadric
  • Hat/cap
  • Taken by Cadric
  • Dumbwaiter
  • Large enough to carry several people
  • Connects to the hidden basement room
  • Bloody footprints found inside
  • Five hanging victims
  • All missing their tongues
  • Most had their throats cut
  • Tunnel to the cistern
  • Jain found only a shoe inside
  • Ladna's unborn creature
  • Multiple eyes
  • Tail
  • Surrounded/protected by several layers of bone
  • Greenish-blue light
  • Appeared at midnight
  • Orbs traveled from Crawford Manor toward it
  • Ghostly baby
  • Ladna carried a baby during the hallowed march even though the creature removed from her body was dead and decidedly not human

docs.title: Questions to Remember
docs.text:
• What are the small white flowers, and why were they growing in the observatory but not the greenhouse?
  • Where exactly does the cistern/tunnel lead?
  • Who were the other murdered people in the basement?
  • Why were their tongues removed?
  • Why was Daverick kept alive?
  • Did Thema truly know nothing about the bodies despite serving at Crawford Manor for 62 years?
  • What caused Sterling's physical transformation?
  • Who did Sterling mean by "them" when he said, "I will not let them take her"?
  • What exactly was growing inside Ladna?
  • Why did Ladna appear at midnight carrying a normal-looking baby?
  • Who is Wilfred Godfroy?
  • What happens at Griffin Hill?
  • What is the hallowed march?
  • What is special about the sapphire necklace?
  • Does Sterling's ring have any significance?
  • What caused the greenish-blue light?
  • Where were Sterling, Ladna, and the baby actually going?

docs.title: Bia's notes - Shaking things up in Waterford
Adventure at a Glance
docs.text:
The party left Crawford behind and headed north toward Waterford, following up on a supply wagon that had disappeared on the road. What began as a search for a wrecked wagon led to monster hunters, a mysterious magical stone, a lucrative contract with Farrow and Thorn, a suspicious portrait recovered from the Argent River, and finally a late-night expedition into the Waterford family mausoleum.

By the end of the night, the party had fought undead beneath the cemetery, robbed more than a few graves, battled animated stone guardians, recovered Lord Waterford's jeweled cane, and reached Level 3.

They also left Waterford with considerably more questions than they started with.

docs.title: Leaving Crawford
docs.text:
• The party spent the night in Crawford following the events at Crawford Manor.
  • Before leaving, Cadric performed “Shake It Off” for Jain, inspired in part by her tendency to shake herself dry.
  • Cadric earned 11 copper in tips.
  • The party headed north toward Waterford.
  • They had also been told to watch for a missing supply wagon traveling between Waterford and Crawford.
  • The road followed Starling Brook north.

docs.title: The Missing Wagon
docs.text:
About two hours into the journey, Jain spotted where a wagon had gone off the road.

The wagon had:

  • gone down an embankment;
  • flipped several times;
  • scattered food, grain, fishing equipment, and other supplies;
  • blood inside;
  • signs that someone had been dragged away.

Jain also found two sets of relatively fresh humanoid footprints and tracks belonging to two hunting dogs.

Among the wreckage was an unusually well-secured crate marked with a raven insignia.

Inside were:

  • children's clothing;
  • medical supplies;
  • sterile needles and other medical equipment;
  • a smaller locked container.

Inside the smaller container was a smooth granite stone about the size of a cue ball, carved with a humanoid face.

The stone was magical.

Jain secretly took it without telling the rest of the party.

docs.title: Following the Tracks
docs.text:
The party followed the tracks from the wagon into the woods and eventually reached a cave.

Inside they discovered the remains of the wagon attack:

  • a badly mauled decaying horse carcass;
  • a human corpse that had been partially eaten;
  • two ghouls and a ghast, already dead.

They also encountered two women and their dogs.

docs.title: Jennifer and Lori
docs.text:
The women introduced themselves as Jennifer and Lori, sisters from Mordenshire who hunt monsters.

  • Jennifer did most of the talking.
  • Lori was noticeably quieter.
  • Their dogs were named Joan and Tiron.
  • The dogs had silver caps on their teeth.

The sisters had been hired by Farrow of Farrow and Thorn to investigate whatever had been attacking travelers in the area.

The evidence indicated that the ghouls and ghast had attacked the wagon and its occupants.

The sisters intended to continue searching the surrounding woods to make sure nothing else dangerous remained.

docs.title: Useful Information
docs.text:
The conversation produced several potentially important leads.

Jennifer and Lori recommended Rudolf Fanbreaking, an herbalist in Mordenshire who supplies equipment useful for hunting monsters.

They also mentioned rumors of a druidic group near Glaston attempting to find a way through the Mists.

When the party discussed eventually traveling toward the area associated with Wilfred Godfrey, Lori offered some very simple advice:

“Get stronger first.”

The sisters' mother is Alice, the mayor of Mordenshire. Her position is an inherited title belonging to her family.

docs.title: Memorable Moment
docs.text:
At some point during all of this, Jain decided to chew on the dead horse.

Because Jain.

docs.title: Waterford
docs.text:
The party continued north and eventually reached Waterford, a considerably larger settlement than Crawford centered around several roads and waterways.

One of its prominent establishments was the Globe Inn.

More importantly, Waterford was home to Farrow and Thorn.

docs.title: A New Job
docs.text:
The party approached Farrow looking for work.

He offered two recovery jobs.

docs.title: Task One — The Portrait
docs.text:
A vessel had wrecked on a sandbar in the Argent River north of Waterford.

Somewhere aboard was a particular portrait Farrow's client wanted recovered.

docs.title: Task Two — Lord Waterford's Cane
docs.text:
The second item was the jeweled walking cane belonging to Lord Waterford.

The cane was believed to be somewhere inside the Waterford family mausoleum.

After Cadric’s negotiation, the party would receive:

180 gp each for each completed task.

Farrow also hinted at a third task.

He refused to tell the party what it was.

They would only learn about it if they successfully completed the first two.

docs.title: The Argent River
docs.text:
The party traveled north along the Argent River until they located the wrecked vessel stranded amid dangerous currents.

Getting aboard required some improvisation involving ropes and Cadric's leather straps.

Once aboard, the party searched the ship.

docs.title: Treasure
docs.text:
Jain found:

  • a gold necklace with an emerald — worth 100 gp;
  • 2 copper;
  • a pristine scimitar.

Cadric found:

  • a silver ring;
  • 200 gp with an invoice addressed to Old Books.

And then they found what they had actually come for.

docs.title: The Portrait
docs.text:
The portrait had been carefully wrapped and protected from the water.

It depicted an unidentified woman.

Something about it was wrong. Jaine saw that the woman's mouth appeared to move.

The party also began questioning whether giving the portrait to Farrow was actually a good idea, and maybe they could get more money returning it to the actual owner.

They brought it back to Waterford anyway—but rather than immediately turning it over, they smuggled it into their room on the top floor of the Globe Inn.

Cadric performed downstairs as a distraction while the portrait was carried upstairs.

For now, the portrait remained with the party.

docs.title: Edgar and the Cemetery
docs.text:
The second contract required getting inside the Waterford family mausoleum.

That meant dealing with Edgar, who worked at the cemetery.

Cadric approached Edgar under the pretense of being interested in purchasing a grave plot for his mother.

During the conversation, the party learned about Idlethorpe, an abandoned settlement southwest of Waterford.

Jeremiah Waterford had apparently been there and encountered something horrifying involving many hands.

The party also learned enough about the cemetery to formulate a plan.

They needed Edgar's keys.

Naturally, they decided to drug him.

docs.title: A Night at the Bar
docs.text:
Cadric brought into the Inn Edgar for a drink.

Jain performed “Jar of Hearts.”

Meanwhile, flowers previously taken from Crawford Manor were slipped into Edgar's drink.

Eventually, Edgar passed out.

The party acquired his keys.

docs.title: The Waterford Mausoleum
docs.text:
At approximately 11:30 p.m., the party entered the Waterford family mausoleum.

Inside they encountered a ghost:

docs.title: Lord Waterford
docs.text:
The spirit was Lord Waterford.

Lord Waterford was aware of disturbances beneath his family's graves and ultimately helped guide the party through the mausoleum.

He also gave them directions to the former Waterford family home.

There was just one problem.

Waterford Manor no longer exists.

Lord Waterford seemed completely unaware of that fact.

docs.title: Beneath the Graves
docs.text:
The party descended beneath the mausoleum into a network of cramped tunnels and burial chambers.

Something had been disturbing the graves.

They eventually heard scraping behind a set of doors and prepared an ambush.

For once, the plan was almost organized.

Two gaunt, fast-moving undead creatures emerged.

Combat followed.

During the exploration and fighting, Jain fell roughly ten feet into the tunnels below and was attacked.

She was eventually reduced to 0 HP and had to be rescued and stabilized.

The party survived the encounter and continued deeper into the Waterford crypts.

docs.title: Grave Robbing with Lord Waterford
docs.text:
Lord Waterford proceeded to identify members of his family buried throughout the crypt.

The party made the decision to rob them.

This created some disagreement about the wisdom—and ethics—of stealing valuables from the Waterford family while the ghost of a Waterford was literally accompanying them.

Nevertheless, the looting began, but only after Lord Waterford retreated to his tomb..

Among the discoveries:

  • Lord Waterford’s cane
  • approximately 200 gp from one tomb;
  • a gold ring;
  • jewelry and necklaces;
  • glasses;
  • a journal;
  • various other valuables.

And then Jaine “accidentally” opened Jeremiah's tomb.

docs.title: The Stone Guardians
docs.text:
The grave robbing eventually led to another problem.

Large stone statues came to life.

The party was forced into another close-quarters battle beneath the mausoleum.

The fight included:

  • Bia raging and engaging the statues in melee;
  • Jain using Hunter's Mark;
  • Cadric using Vicious Mockery;
  • the party using a Dagger of Disintegration, which proved particularly useful against stone.

The statues were eventually destroyed, crumbling into rubble and dust.

The party survived—barely.

docs.title: Lord Waterford's Cane
docs.text:
With the guardians defeated, the party was able to continue searching the crypts.

Eventually they found the second item Farrow had hired them to retrieve:

Lord Waterford's jeweled cane.

The cane had:

  • a large ruby;
  • an obsidian tip;
  • gold plating.

The party had now successfully recovered both items Farrow requested.

Whether Farrow would actually receive both of them was another question.

And then they searched Jeremiah’s crypt.

Inside was a large magical weapon.

Bia's New Weapon

Bia took Jeremiah Waterford's magical +1 great axe from Jeremiah Waterford's tomb.

docs.title: The Portrait Mystery
docs.text:
Several discoveries during the night made the portrait increasingly suspicious.

The woman in the portrait remains unidentified.

However, the party knows that Lady Waterford's grave is empty.

This has led to the theory that the woman depicted in the portrait might be Lady Waterford.

That has not been confirmed.

There is another complication.

Jain knows something the others don't.

Jain knows the portrait is supposed to be taken:

“Home.”

But Lord Waterford believes the Waterford family home still exists.

It doesn't.

That leaves Jain—and eventually perhaps the rest of the party—with no clear idea where the portrait actually wants to go.

docs.title: End of the Night
docs.text:
After surviving the mausoleum, the party returned to the Globe Inn, cleaned themselves up, and took a long rest.

Most importantly:

docs.title: Everyone reached Level 3.
docs.text: New subclasses and abilities await the party before their next adventure.

docs.title: The Woman in the Portrait
docs.text: Who is she, and why did her mouth move?

docs.title: Lady Waterford
docs.text: Why is Lady Waterford's tomb empty? Is the woman in the portrait Lady Waterford?

docs.title: “Take Me Home”
docs.text: Only Jain knows the portrait is supposed to go “home.” What does that mean when Waterford Manor no longer exists?

docs.title: The Missing Manor
docs.text: Why does Lord Waterford apparently have no idea that his family's home is gone? He’d been dead for maybe 60 years? What happened to Waterford Manor and how long ago?

docs.title: Lady Waterford's Body
docs.text: If the portrait depicts Lady Waterford, does the party need to find her remains? Does “home” mean returning her—or the portrait—to the Waterford family tomb?

docs.title: Farrow's Third Task
docs.text: What is the task Farrow refused to reveal? Could it have something to do with Lady Waterford, the portrait, or her missing body?

docs.title: The Magical Face Stone
docs.text: What exactly did Jain take from the raven-marked medical shipment—and why was someone transporting it toward Crawford?

docs.title: Idlethorpe
docs.text: What happened to the abandoned settlement, and what did Jeremiah encounter there involving all those hands?

docs.title: The Mists
docs.text: Who are the druids near Glaston, and are they really trying to find a way through the Mists?

docs.title: Bia's notes - Home is where the horrors are
Adventure at a glance
docs.text:
• Investigated Lady Waterford’s past and learned that she was born a DeLawrence Pouchenelle and came from Idlethorp.
  • Followed Lady Waterford’s portrait to the abandoned town of Idlethorp and her family’s ruined manor.
  • Fought grotesque creatures made from stitched-together body parts and discovered they were connected to a living brain in a jar.
  • Encountered a huge stitched man who resisted whatever was controlling him long enough to remove the bolts from his neck. His final word was “Sister.”
  • Returned Lady Waterford’s portrait to its place among the DeLawrence Pouchenelle family portraits.
  • Bia destroyed the brain, causing the remaining stitched creatures to collapse.
  • Looted several magic items and potions before Jain burned down the manor.
  • Returned to Farrow and received 90 gp each as partial payment.
  • Learned Farrow’s mysterious third job may have involved retrieving the very brain Bia had just destroyed.
  • Left Waterford and headed toward Candle Cross, where the castle drawbridge reportedly moves on its own.

docs.title: Waterford
docs.text:
• Still trying to figure out what Lady Waterford meant when she told Jain she wanted to go home.
  • Jain stayed in room 301 with the portrait.
  • Cadric questioned Edgar.
  • Elisandra and I talked to Renee, who owns the Globe Inn.
  • Learned:
  • Lord and Lady Waterford died in a carriage accident 64 years ago.
  • They were traveling toward Mordenshire for a gala at Godfroy's Manor.
  • Lady Waterford was a DeLawrence Pouchenelle before marrying Lord Waterford.
  • Her family was from Idlethorp.
  • Edgar checks the Waterford mausoleum regularly. There is a sealed coffin for Lady Waterford, but he has never opened it.
  • We already know her coffin is empty. So where is her body?

docs.title: Scarred ghost
docs.text:
• While Jain was alone in room 301, a scarred man came into the room.
  • He seemed surprised to find Jain there.
  • Then he walked through the wall.
  • Jain saw him heading toward the docks.
  • I stayed with Lady Waterford's portrait while everyone else went after him.
  • They found a secret gathering place under the Globe Inn. We called it the human speakeasy.
  • Didn't figure out who the scarred man was, but the group did recognize one of the ghosts as one who was in Henry Loust’s office.

docs.title: Idlethorp
docs.text:
• Headed to Idlethorp because that might be the "home" Lady Waterford wanted.
  • Red warning flags outside town.
  • Met Dave, who was warning travelers away.
  • Town has been abandoned for about 6 weeks.
  • Strange noises and shadowy creatures at night.
  • Another group went in about a week ago. Only one came back.
  • We camped outside town instead of going in at night.
  • I suggested taking out Lady Waterford's portrait to see if she reacted.
  • Jain touched the frame and suddenly ran toward the manor with the portrait.
  • She wasn't controlling herself and didn't remember running there afterward.

docs.title: Creatures in Idlethorp
docs.text:
• Attacked by creatures made from stitched-together human body parts.
  • Cadric used Daylight.
  • The creatures hated it and fled.
  • They all ran toward the DeLawrence Pouchenelle manor.

docs.title: DeLawrence Pouchenelle Manor
docs.text:
• Jain pressed Lady Waterford's portrait against the manor and asked if this was the home she wanted.
  • Jain felt warmth/contentment. Definitely the right place.

docs.title: Giant stitched man
docs.text:
• Found a stitched humanoid over 8 feet tall.
  • Two metal bolts sticking out of his neck.
  • He attacked us.
  • Elisandra spoke to him telepathically about Lady Waterford and the DeLawrence Pouchenelle family.
  • He seemed to recognize something.
  • Electricity came from the bolts and seemed to take control again.
  • Elisandra told him the bolts might be controlling him.
  • He pulled both bolts out himself.
  • Electricity arced through him.
  • He collapsed and said "Sister."
  • He died.
  • Thick, dark red sludge came out of him instead of normal blood.
  • Who was he? Whose sister was he remembering? Lady Waterford?

docs.title: Meanwhile, Jain...
docs.text:
• Jain ended up alone in the ruined ballroom.
  • Huge pile of wagons, crates, lumber, dead horses, body parts, etc.
  • Watched a torso creature crawl into the pile.
  • Jain actually decided NOT to investigate it.
  • This seems important enough to document.
  • Instead, she investigated the fireplace.
  • Found a pressure-activated hook above the fireplace mantel.
  • Climbed up and triggered it.
  • Opened a secret passage.
  • Went inside by herself, because apparently the good judgment had worn off.

docs.title: Secret rooms / laboratory
docs.text:
• Cadric picked a lock.
  • Swinging blade dropped from the ceiling and barely missed his head.
  • Heard a voice say: "Don't disturb him while he's working."
  • Found a library/laboratory.
  • Man working over the body of a dwarf with surgical tools.
  • Leon DeLawrence Pouchenelle — Lady Waterford's brother.
  • Also: living brain in a jar.
  • Brain attacked me psychically.
  • More stitched creatures surrounded us.

docs.title: Ravenlost vs. the brain
docs.text:
• I eventually smashed the brain's jar with my axe.
  • Brain exploded.
  • All of the remaining stitched creatures collapsed.
  • Apparently the brain was controlling/animating them.
  • At the time, destroying the evil brain seemed like an excellent idea.

docs.title: Jain returns
docs.text:
• Jain came out through a bookcase connected to her secret fireplace passage.
  • Lots of dismembered body parts everywhere after the brain died.
  • Jain picked up two hands/arms.
  • Waved them around at Cadric.
  • A ring flew off one.
  • Cadric decided not to go after it and called it "the angel's share."
  • Jain then used the corpse arms to hug Cadric.

docs.title: Lady Waterford
docs.text:
• Found a wall filled with DeLawrence Pouchenelle family portraits.
  • One empty spot.
  • Lady Waterford's portrait fit perfectly.
  • Jain put her back with her family.
  • Jain felt the warmth/contentment settle. Lady Waterford finally seemed satisfied.
  • Still don't know where Lady Waterford's body is.

docs.title: Magic items
docs.text:
• Cadric
  • Cloak of Many Fashions
  • Instrument of Illusions
  • Bia
  • Boots of False Tracks
  • Elisandra
  • Eyes of Minute Seeing

docs.title: Potions
docs.text:
• Cadric — Potion of Growth
  • Bia — Potion of Giant Strength
  • Elisandra — Potion of Fire Breathing
  • Jain
  • Potion of Animal Friendship
  • Potion of Resistance
  • Scent of the Mists

Jain identified the potions by tasting them. Of course she did.

docs.title: Goodbye, manor
docs.text:
• Jain set the manor on fire.
  • Left Idlethorp and headed back to Waterford.

docs.title: Farrow
docs.text:
• Returned to collect our reward.
  • We were supposed to retrieve:
  • Lady Waterford's portrait.
  • Lord Waterford's jeweled walking stick.
  • We returned with neither, as far as Farrow knows.
  • Portrait stayed at the DeLawrence Pouchenelle manor.
  • Got 90 gp each as partial payment.
  • Farrow finally told us about the third job:
  • Client wants an object of power.
  • Small enough to fit in a hand.
  • We'd know it when we saw it.
  • We think it might have been the brain.
  • The brain I smashed.
  • Oops.

docs.title: Next: Candle Cross
docs.text:
• Leaving Waterford.
  • Heading toward Mordenshire through Candle Cross.
  • Candle Cross is built in the ruins of an old castle along the Arden River.
  • Its drawbridge supposedly raises and lowers by itself.
  • Some people think it reacts when evil threatens the town.

docs.title: Discoveries
docs.text: • Glim Brightstone connection: The clockwork ballerina on the fountain in the DeLawrence Pouchenelle manor had a plaque that read, “For my friend of a like mind, happy birthday, Glim Brightstone.” Someone in this family knew Glim personally. We later found a dwarf body in the laboratory. We still don’t know whether that dwarf was Glim, or who Glim’s mysterious assistant was.

docs.title: Things we still don't know
docs.text:
• Where is Lady Waterford's body?
  • Who was the scarred ghost in room 301?
  • Who was the giant stitched man, and who did he mean by "Sister"?
  • What exactly was happening in the DeLawrence Pouchenelle laboratory?
  • Was the dwarf on the lab table Glim Brightstone?
  • Was the brain actually the object Farrow's client wanted?
  • Who is Farrow's client?
  • What happens if Farrow finds out we destroyed the object?
  • What's controlling the drawbridge at Candle Cross?
